ai.heading: AI integration
ai.description: Claude Code connects straight to this app's database. Start it on your computer and it reaches the same todos, schedule, notes and dailies these screens show, through the MCP server. The app itself never calls an AI.
ai.activityValue: A briefing is written in the daily for {{date}}.

ai.activityCaveat: Read from the "Briefing" heading in your dailies. Anything you typed there yourself counts the same way.
ai.launchDescription: Opens a terminal running `claude` in the folder below. That folder is what decides the connection: Claude Code reads the MCP server out of the project's .mcp.json, so starting it anywhere else gives you a Claude that cannot see this app's data.
ai.pathPlaceholder: The full path to the life-editor folder
ai.launched: A terminal opened. Claude Code is starting there.
ai.desktopOnly: Available in the desktop app. Claude Code is a program on your computer, so the browser and the phone app have nothing to start.
ai.errorInvalidPath: No folder at that path. Give the full path, starting from the top of the drive.
ai.errorNotFound: Could not find Claude Code on this computer. Install it, then try again.
ai.errorSpawnFailed: The terminal would not open. Nothing was started.
ai.errorUnavailable: This build of the desktop app cannot start Claude Code yet.

launcher.title: Welcome to Life Editor
launcher.intro: Life Editor is one place to plan a day and to record it. Check what is coming up in the morning, look back on it at night.
launcher.pickerTitle: What would you like to be shown?
launcher.pickerIntro: Pick a section and the tutorial opens it and starts there. Sections the tutorial does not cover yet cannot be picked.
launcher.full: Walk the whole tutorial from the start
launcher.fullDescription: Every section in order, beginning at step one.

summary.briefing: The day on one page: what is coming up, and what you said you would do.
summary.schedule: Your calendar and your todos, side by side on the time axis.
summary.materials: Notes and daily entries — the things you write and come back to.

steps.briefingIntro: This is the Briefing — the day on one page. You do not write it: Claude Code fills it in through the desktop app's MCP connection. On the web on its own it stays empty, which is normal rather than broken.
steps.scheduleCreateEvent: Start here to put something on the calendar. Add one event — the tour waits until it exists, not until you press the button.
steps.scheduleAdjustEvent: Open the event you just made and change its time. Plans move; this is how you move them.
steps.scheduleOpenTodos: Todos live in the same section as the calendar. Open the Todo tab.
steps.scheduleCreateTodo: Add a todo — something you want done, without deciding when yet.
steps.scheduleCompleteTodo: Finish it. Tick it off in the tray, or open it and switch its status.
steps.materialsCapture: Add something here. Todos, notes and daily entries all start from this one button.
steps.materialsNoteBody: Write a few words. The body saves as you type — there is no save button to remember.
steps.materialsNoteTag: Give it a tag. Tags are how a note joins everything else about the same thing.
steps.materialsTagFollow: Pick a tag here to see only what carries it — that is how you get back to related notes later.
